parameters.name: bgwriter_delay
parameters.meaning: Delay between background-writer rounds.

parameters.name: bgwriter_flush_after
parameters.meaning: Amount written by the background writer before requesting operating-system writeback.

parameters.name: bgwriter_lru_maxpages
parameters.meaning: Maximum buffers written per background-writer round.

parameters.name: bgwriter_lru_multiplier
parameters.meaning: Multiplier on recent buffer demand used to estimate background cleaning needs.

parameters.name: checkpoint_completion_target
parameters.meaning: Fraction of the checkpoint interval over which checkpoint writes are spread.

parameters.name: checkpoint_flush_after
parameters.meaning: Amount written during a checkpoint before requesting operating-system writeback.

parameters.name: checkpoint_timeout
parameters.meaning: Maximum interval between automatic WAL checkpoints.

parameters.name: commit_siblings
parameters.meaning: Minimum concurrent open transactions considered before applying commit_delay.

parameters.name: deadlock_timeout
parameters.meaning: Lock-wait interval before checking for a deadlock.

parameters.name: default_statistics_target
parameters.meaning: Default target controlling the detail of collected column statistics.

parameters.name: effective_cache_size
parameters.meaning: Planner estimate of cache available to a query; does not allocate memory.

parameters.name: effective_io_concurrency
parameters.meaning: Estimated concurrent disk I/O operations supported by the storage system.

parameters.name: min_wal_size
parameters.meaning: Lower WAL disk-usage threshold below which old WAL files are recycled for reuse.

parameters.name: random_page_cost
parameters.meaning: Planner cost estimate for a nonsequential disk-page read.

parameters.name: seq_page_cost
parameters.meaning: Planner cost estimate for a sequential disk-page read.

parameters.name: temp_buffers
parameters.meaning: Per-session buffer limit for access to temporary tables.

parameters.name: wal_buffers
parameters.meaning: Shared buffer space for WAL data; physical value -1 selects automatic sizing.

parameters.name: wal_sync_method
parameters.meaning: Operating-system method used to force WAL updates to disk.

parameters.name: wal_writer_delay
parameters.meaning: Delay between WAL-writer activity rounds.

parameters.name: work_mem
parameters.meaning: Base memory limit per sort or hash operation before spilling to temporary disk files.

prior_facts: Settings cover memory and caching, I/O, concurrency, query optimization, logging, replication, and authentication. Increasing every resource setting is not a general improvement rule.
Some settings apply only to particular storage engines or enabled features; some are legacy settings. A parameter's real database meaning does not establish its importance in this surrogate.
The available materials do not specify the full hardware and database-version configuration used to train the surrogate. Do not assume every described mechanism is active in this workload.
units_policy: Use the units in this task's parameter definitions. Do not invent unit conversions for entries without an explicit unit.
background: Tune 20 PostgreSQL settings for a JOB analytical join-query workload to minimize predicted query latency. A fixed, previously built surrogate predicts performance; optimization does not execute a live database workload.
input_instructions: Submit all 20 settings as floating-point numbers u in [0,1]. Names identify real database settings, but physical values and enumeration labels from the table must not be submitted directly.
For integer settings, decode as round(min + u*(max-min)). For physical floating-point settings, decode as min + u*(max-min) without rounding.

For K enumeration options, divide [0,1] into K equal-width intervals. Select enum_values[min(floor(u*K),K-1)] using zero-based indexing; u=1 selects the last option. Option order does not imply a performance ranking.
Encoding example: bgwriter_delay has physical range 10...10000; input 0.25 decodes to 2508. This illustrates encoding, not a recommended configuration.
Enumeration example: for wal_sync_method, input 0 selects "fsync", and 1 selects "open_datasync". The order is part of the encoding, not a performance ranking.
evaluation_details: The evaluator decodes inputs and returns surrogate-predicted latency; lower is better.
Use the ranges, defaults, and enumeration order in this task's parameter table. A default is a reference configuration value, not a known optimum.
domain_knowledge: effective_cache_size and page-cost settings influence planner estimates; they do not allocate cache or directly change disk speed. A changed estimate can select a different query plan.
More work_mem may reduce sort or hash spills, but this is a per-operation budget. Several operations and sessions can consume it concurrently.
WAL buffers and checkpoint pacing concern logging and background I/O. Their benefit depends on workload and storage conditions; the surrogate response must test any proposed direction.
JOB contains analytical joins. Statistics, memory, caching, and plan selection can interact, so parameter changes need not produce smooth latency changes.
